analysis:
The PR changes only test expectations and one comment in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/NemotronSuperServingPolicyTests.swift. It touches defaultBankFollowsTheGrantWithinItsBounds (lines ~297-305) and defaultBankFollowsTheChunkAndYieldsToTheOperator (line ~324). Default prefix bank expectations drop: 34 GiB grant 3 GiB -> 2.5 GiB (12<<28 -> 10<<28), 45 GiB 8.5 -> 8 GiB (34<<28 -> 32<<28), 50 GiB narrow chunk 11 -> 10.5 GiB, wide 14.5 -> 13.5 GiB. Each bank shrinks by half of 1 GiB, 0.5 GiB, 0.5 GiB and 1 GiB. This implies a production sizing change, probably an extra reserve deducted from the slack, but the sizing source (NemotronSuperServingPolicy.defaultPrefixBankBytes) is not in the supplied evidence. The test changes alter no runtime security behavior.

Relevant threat: T-041 (prefix cache). A smaller default in-memory bank leaves the SSD tier, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, salt scoping and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch untouched. It slightly reduces the cache footprint and the memory-pressure/availability risk. The remaining assertions in the file still check the 16 GiB cap, the quarter-of-grant bound, monotonicity, the 2x-slack bound and the operator override, so the bounds invariants are retained. The test-side change lowers expectations, which does not weaken the bounds checks. The next pass should confirm that the corresponding source change keeps the bank within the load-claim and admission bounds, since it is not in this batch.
